newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee falls vs spot dlr, gains in forwards.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee falls vs spot dlr, gains in forwards.

text.p: Spot rupee fell sharply to 35.94/96 against the dollar on Thursday under the onslaught of dollar buying by local banks and a Calcutta bank, dealers said.
Spot dollar had opened the day at 35.89/90 per dollar.
The rupee came under pressure early in the day from genuine import demand, spearheaded mainly by foreign banks, pulling down the Indian currency to 35.91 from 35.89 opening, dealers said.
"Then he came in and hit each of us," said a dealer, referring to the Calcutta-based state-run bank.
Many dealers said the bank could have been buying on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) which is facing redemption of India Development Bonds worth $1.8 billion on February 15.
The Calcutta bank's foray led to frenzy with some banks speculating that RBI would sell dollars to prevent the rupee from hitting the 36.0 per dollar mark. But this did not happen.
The last hour of trading saw banks - every one of them - already short on dollars scrambling to build positions, taking the rupee to the day's low of 35.96, dealers said.
The rupee continued to gain against the forward dollar on the back of RBI's dollar purchases in swap deals, dealer said.
August dollars slipped to 1.33/1.36 rupees at close from 1.38/1.41 opening level because of RBI's swaps, they said.
"But it was more noise than action," said a dealer. "Their actual intervention could not have been more than $35 million, but their persistent enquiries conveyed stronger intervention."
Many dealers expect the RBI to resume dollar buying on Friday ahead of the IDB redemption scheduled for Saturday.
